title: Adjournment motion on return-to-work support for injured and ill workers
what_it_is: An adjournment motion in which Mr Melvin Yong spoke on strengthening return-to-work support for injured and ill workers, and the Minister of State for Manpower responded.
why_it_matters: The transcript records proposals to strengthen return-to-work support and a planned MOM review, but it does not state any immediate change to entitlements or support for workers. MOM says it will launch an Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity in the second half of 2026. The record does not set out the practical impact of these steps.

key_points.point: Ms Indranee Rajah moved that Parliament adjourn.
key_points.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
key_points.quote: That Parliament do now adjourn.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong said Singapore recorded 660 major workplace injuries in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: In 2025, Singapore recorded 660 major workplace injuries.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong said return-to-work must be treated as a core pillar of the workforce system.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: return-to-work must be treated as a core pillar of our workforce system, not a secondary consideration.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong said leading jurisdictions share three principles: early intervention, shared responsibility and workplace-centred solutions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: Across these systems, three principles stand out: early intervention, shared responsibility and workplace-centred solutions.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong proposed strengthening early intervention through earlier referral, clearer employer expectations and early coordination.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: We should therefore strengthen early intervention by encouraging earlier referral into return-to-work support; establishing clearer expectations for employer engagement; and promoting early coordination between employers, workers, insurers and healthcare practitioners.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong said the forthcoming Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity intends to explore industry-led solutions to promote return-to-work.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: I am therefore glad that the forthcoming Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity intends to explore industry-led solutions to promote return-to-work.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong said SMEs employ around 70% of the local workforce.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: SMEs employ around 70% of our local workforce today.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong said NTUC, MOM and SNEF are developing the Tripartite Advisory on Providing Reasonable Accommodations to Persons with Disabilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: NTUC, together with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF), is developing the Tripartite Advisory on Providing Reasonable Accommodations to Persons with Disabilities.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong urged the Ministry to consider expanding the advisory or introducing a complementary one to cover workers recovering from injuries and serious health conditions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: I urge the Ministry to consider expanding this advisory or, perhaps, introducing a complementary one – to explicitly cover workers recovering from injuries and serious health conditions.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong proposed a dedicated Back-to-Work pathway for workers unable to return to their previous jobs due to illness or injury.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: I propose that we develop a dedicated Back-to-Work pathway that supports workers who are unable to return to their previous jobs due to illness or injury.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong suggested a time-bound wage support scheme to help employers reintegrate workers recovering from serious health conditions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: I therefore suggest that the Government consider introducing a time-bound wage support scheme to help employers reintegrate workers recovering from serious health conditions.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong suggested allowing MediSave to be used for return-to-work-related expenses such as assessments and evaluations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: Allowing MediSave to be used for return-to-work-related expenses, such as assessments and evaluations of a worker's condition and fitness for work.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said survey data over the past five years showed about 3,800 unemployed residents had left previous jobs due to health-related reasons.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: over the past five years, there were about 3,800 unemployed residents who had left their previous jobs due to health-related reasons.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said MOM conducted a pilot with the Workplace Safety and Health Council from 2017 to 2021 to establish return-to-work capabilities in seven public hospitals.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: MOM conducted a pilot with the Workplace Safety and Health Council (WSHC) from 2017 to 2021 to establish return-to-work capabilities in seven public hospitals.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said the pilot enrolled 3,700 workers whose employers were committed to supporting their participation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The pilot enrolled a total of 3,700 workers whose employers were committed to supporting their participation in the programme.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said the pilot enabled 95% of those workers to successfully return to work.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: enabled 95% of these workers to successfully return to work.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said return-to-work expenses for work-related injuries are claimable under the Work Injury Compensation Act.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: For work-related injuries, such return-to-work expenses are claimable under the Work Injury Compensation Act.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said the Ministry of Health rolled out an inter-agency pilot called the Bounce Back Lab from 2023 to 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: the Ministry of Health rolled out an inter-agency pilot called the "Bounce Back Lab" from 2023 to 2025.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said the Ministry will conduct a review of the return-to-work landscape and will consider the Member's suggestions carefully.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The Ministry will be conducting a review of the return-to-work landscape in Singapore and will consider the Member's suggestions carefully.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said MOM is looking to partner with industry and crowdsource innovative ideas to improve return-to-work outcomes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: MOM is looking to partner with the industry and crowdsource innovative ideas to improve return-to-work outcomes.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said MOM will launch the Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity with NTUC and SNEF in the second half of 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we will be launching an Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity (AfA-SHEL) together with NTUC and SNEF in the second half of 2026.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said the AfA-SHEL will catalyse ground-up solutions and facilitating injured workers back to work is one focus area.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The AfA-SHEL will catalyse ground-up solutions to common workplace safety risks and concerns, and facilitating injured workers back to work is one of our focus areas.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash said proposals could include job redesign, SME capability building and new partnership models matching workers to jobs based on functional abilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: proposals could include innovative job redesign approaches for common injuries or health conditions, initiatives to build SMEs' capabilities in supporting return-to-work, or new partnership models that better match workers to jobs, based on their functional abilities.

key_points.point: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash encouraged the public to participate in the ground-up solutions later in the year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: We encourage the public to participate in these ground-up solutions later in the year.

key_points.point: Mr Deputy Speaker informed Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.00 pm.
key_points.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
key_points.quote: the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.00 pm.

key_points.point: Parliament adjourned at 7.37 pm.
key_points.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
key_points.quote: Adjourned accordingly at 7.37 pm.

what_happens_next: Parliament adjourned at 7.37 pm. The next sitting is tomorrow at 12.00 pm. MOM will conduct a review of the return-to-work landscape, and will launch the Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity with NTUC and SNEF in the second half of 2026; the public is encouraged to participate in ground-up solutions later in the year.
not_said: Whether the Tripartite Advisory on Providing Reasonable Accommodations to Persons with Disabilities will be expanded or complemented to cover workers recovering from injuries and serious health conditions.
Whether a dedicated Back-to-Work pathway will be established.
Whether a time-bound wage support scheme will be introduced.
Whether MediSave will be allowed for return-to-work-related expenses.
What specific changes the MOM review of the return-to-work landscape will produce.
How the Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity will select and scale prototypes.
Whether the AfA-SHEL's focus on injured workers will extend to workers with non-work-related conditions.
What funding or support will be available for SMEs to implement work accommodations.
How the 3,800 figure relates to the 660 major workplace injuries in 2025.
Whether the next sitting at 12.00 pm will include further debate on this matter.
